trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide: The platinum unlocks when the other 54 trophies are earned — there is no separate task behind it. Work the six roadmap stages in order and this one lands last, after 100% completion.

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.missableReason: Tied to the opening mission Gone Fishing — earn it on your first run through the story; the official description does not say the mission can be replayed.
trophies.guide: Finish the opening mission, Gone Fishing, which is the first mission of the story, so this trophy comes in the opening hour. Play through the mission's objectives as the game presents them. No extra step is pinned down by the official description.

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.missableReason: Tied to Chapter 1 — finish it when the story brings you there; the official description does not say a chapter can be replayed.
trophies.guide: Finish Chapter 1 in full. A chapter ends when its last mission is done, so keep playing the story missions in order and this lands on its own. Nothing beyond the chapter's missions is pinned down by the official description.

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.missableReason: Tied to Chapter 2 — finish it when the story brings you there; the official description does not say a chapter can be replayed.
trophies.guide: Finish Chapter 2 in full, the same way as Chapter 1: play its story missions in order until the chapter closes. No extra step is pinned down by the official description.

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.missableReason: Tied to Chapter 3 — finish it when the story brings you there; the official description does not say a chapter can be replayed.
trophies.guide: Finish Chapter 3 in full by playing its story missions in order. The name says it all: this is the chapter where Vice City itself takes centre stage. Nothing beyond the chapter's missions is pinned down by the official description.

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.missableReason: Tied to Chapter 4 — finish it when the story brings you there; the official description does not say a chapter can be replayed.
trophies.guide: Finish Chapter 4 in full by playing its story missions in order. This is the last numbered chapter before the finale, so the story missions here are the run-up to the end. No extra step is pinned down by the official description.

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.missableReason: Tied to the final mission — it happens once, at the end of the story; the official description does not say the finale can be replayed.
trophies.guide: Finish the final mission of the story. This is the only gold trophy in the story line and it closes the main plot, so play it when the game offers it — there is no later story mission to fall back on. Which choices the finale offers is not pinned down by the official description, so follow the mission as presented.

trophies.name: Trust
trophies.missableReason: Tied to the story mission Breakfast Run — earn it when the mission comes up; the official description does not say it can be replayed.
trophies.guide: Finish the story mission Breakfast Run. It is one of the named story missions, so it arrives in the mission order and unlocks when the mission's objectives are done. No extra step is pinned down by the official description.

trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.missableReason: Tied to the story mission The Cartel Heist — earn it when the mission comes up; the official description does not say it can be replayed.
trophies.guide: Finish the story mission The Cartel Heist. Heists in this game are set-piece missions, so follow the plan the game lays out and finish the job. No extra step is pinned down by the official description.

trophies.name: Family Matters
trophies.missableReason: Tied to the story mission Child's Play — earn it when the mission comes up; the official description does not say it can be replayed.
trophies.guide: Finish the story mission Child's Play. It arrives in the story's mission order, so keep playing the main missions and it will come to you. No extra step is pinned down by the official description.

trophies.name: DWNFALL
trophies.missableReason: Tied to the story mission Headliners — earn it when the mission comes up; the official description does not say it can be replayed.
trophies.guide: Finish the story mission Headliners. Like the other named story missions it arrives in order, so play the main missions through and finish its objectives. No extra step is pinned down by the official description.

trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
trophies.missableReason: Tied to the story mission VCIA Takedown — earn it when the mission comes up; the official description does not say it can be replayed.
trophies.guide: Finish the story mission VCIA Takedown, set around the airport. Take the mission down as the game directs it and the trophy follows the mission's completion. No extra step is pinned down by the official description.

trophies.name: Snow Storm
trophies.missableReason: Tied to the story mission Operation Savage Glory — earn it when the mission comes up; the official description does not say it can be replayed.
trophies.guide: Finish the story mission Operation Savage Glory. It is the last of the named story missions in the list, so it sits late in the mission order. No extra step is pinned down by the official description.

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide: Reach 100% completion, which the game tracks across story, stranger strands, activities, collectibles and the rest — the second gold trophy and the last one before the platinum. Treat it as a checklist: this guide's roadmap stages 1 to 5 are the work that fills the percentage. Exactly what counts toward the 100% is not pinned down by the official description, so use the in-game stats screen as the authority and mop up whatever it still lists.

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide: Pull off 250 stunts — jumps, near misses, drifts and the like, whatever the game counts as a stunt. It is a grind, not a skill test: stunt whenever the chance comes up while driving between missions and the count climbs. Which moves the game counts is not pinned down by the official description, so watch the in-game stunt counter and favour whatever it credits.

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Try each type of activity once — the list tracks 9 activity types, so sample one of each: a race, a fishing trip, an arcade game, a drone race, a shooting range session and the rest of the set. This is a taster trophy: one go at each is enough, and it pairs naturally with the other activity trophies. The full list of the 9 types is not pinned down by the official description, so tick them off as the game's activity menu offers them.

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Earn a gold medal in all 42 Shooting Range challenges — the count the official list tracks. Work through the range's challenge set weapon by weapon, replaying any challenge that lands silver until it turns gold. A gold here is a score target, not a one-off, so retries cost nothing but time. Which weapons each challenge uses is not pinned down by the official description.

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun drone race at every one of the 14 locations the list tracks. Each location is its own race, so visit them all and take first place at each — a win anywhere else does not cover a location you have not raced. The 14 locations themselves are not pinned down by the official description, so use the in-game map markers for the drone races.

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.guide: Win 20 different races — different courses count, repeats of one course do not. Mix race types and locations as you go so the distinct count climbs, and keep an eye on which courses you have already won. The race roster itself is not pinned down by the official description, so the in-game race list is the authority on what is left.

trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge. Fishing challenges are head-to-head, so out-fish Cal in the challenge the game offers — land the better catch or the bigger haul, however that challenge scores it. If you lose, the challenge can be tried again; the description names no one-time window. Where and when Cal's challenge appears is not pinned down by the official description.

trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
trophies.guide: Complete one arcade game, start to finish. Find an arcade cabinet, pick any game on it and play it through to its end — a single completion is all it takes. Which cabinets and games exist is not pinned down by the official description, so any arcade game you can finish counts.

trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.missableReason: Tied to Andy's final mission — finish the strand when it comes up; the official description does not say the strand can be replayed.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission for Andy, the last step of his side strand. Side strands open as you meet their characters in the world, so follow Andy's missions through to their end. How many missions his strand holds is not pinned down by the official description — the in-game mission list for Andy is the guide.

trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.missableReason: Tied to Kenton's final mission — finish the strand when it comes up; the official description does not say the strand can be replayed.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission for Kenton, the last step of his side strand. Follow Kenton's missions through to their end as they appear in the world. How many missions his strand holds is not pinned down by the official description.

trophies.name: The Lone Rider
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.missableReason: Tied to Billy's final mission — finish the strand when it comes up; the official description does not say the strand can be replayed.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission for Billy, the last step of his side strand. Follow Billy's missions through to their end as they appear in the world. How many missions his strand holds is not pinned down by the official description.

trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across Leonida — the count the official list tracks. Strangers appear as markers in the world, each with their own little strand; finish any 8 of them. The five named-character finales in this guide (Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone) are part of the same idea, so the strands you finish for them count toward the 8. Which strangers exist beyond those five is not pinned down by the official description.

trophies.name: Supply & Demand
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.missableReason: Tied to Randy's final mission — finish the strand when it comes up; the official description does not say the strand can be replayed.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission for Randy, the last step of his side strand. Follow Randy's missions through to their end as they appear in the world. How many missions his strand holds is not pinned down by the official description.

trophies.name: Spin On This!
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.missableReason: Tied to Tyrone's final mission — finish the strand when it comes up; the official description does not say the strand can be replayed.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission for Tyrone, the last step of his side strand. Follow Tyrone's missions through to their end as they appear in the world. How many missions his strand holds is not pinned down by the official description.

trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Meditate at every spot across Leonida — the list tracks 18 meditation spots. Visit each one and meditate there; the spots stay available, so this is a sightseeing tour rather than a race. Where the 18 spots are is not pinned down by the official description, so use the in-game map and any spot markers the game shows.

trophies.name: Fair Game
trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Hunt a unique animal for Bret — one specific animal, hunted for one specific person. Bret's strand will point you at the animal when it is time; track it and take it down. Which animal it is and where it roams is not pinned down by the official description, so follow Bret's missions rather than guessing.

trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
trophies.guide: Complete 3 collectible card sets — the count the official list tracks. Cards are scattered across Leonida, so pick up every card you pass and finish any 3 full sets. Cards stay where they are until collected, so nothing here can be missed. How many cards each set holds is not pinned down by the official description.

trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
trophies.guide: WAiNK It at 100 locations — the count the official list tracks. WAiNK is the game's in-world photo-sharing gag, so the job is to trigger it at 100 distinct spots across the map, a little at a time as you travel. Locations stay available, so this is a long slow grind, not a timed one. What counts as a WAiNK location is not pinned down by the official description beyond the count.

trophies.name: One Last Thing
trophies.guide: Complete 50 challenges — the count the official list tracks. Challenges are the game's small side goals, spread across driving, combat, exploration and the rest, so they pile up naturally while you chase the other trophies. Check the in-game challenges menu to see which are close to done and finish the easy ones first. The full challenge list is not pinned down by the official description.

trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: Lose a 4-star wanted level with your partner beside you and escape the heat. Build the wanted level to 4 stars while your partner is with you, then break line of sight and stay out of the search area until it clears. It can be tried again any time your partner is around, so a failed escape costs nothing. How the partner joins you for free roam is not pinned down by the official description.

trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your wanted level — the trick is keeping the wanted level alive across all three robberies, not losing it. Pick three shops close together, rob them one after another with your partner along, and keep the heat on until the third is done. It can be retried freely. Which shops count is not pinned down by the official description.

trophies.name: Whip It Good
trophies.guide: Discover 100 vehicles — the count the official list tracks. Every new vehicle type you get into counts, so drive anything you have not driven before and the total climbs as you explore. Vehicles stay in the world, so nothing here can be missed. The full vehicle roster is not pinned down by the official description.

trophies.name: Gunslinger
trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus. Set it up where enemies cluster — a wanted-level shootout with plenty of police around is the obvious stage — then trigger Combat Focus and drop five before it ends. It can be retried as often as you like. How Combat Focus is charged is not pinned down by the official description.

trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA, the airport — leave by a route the airport did not schedule, in a plane or otherwise. The description is deliberately vague, so the spirit is a getaway from the airfield rather than a ticketed flight. It can be tried again any time. What exactly counts as the departure is not pinned down by the official description.

trophies.name: Challenging Tank
trophies.guide: The description is a joke with a hint: Rhinos are the game's tanks, and the heat is the point. Get into a Rhino tank — most likely by stealing one once the wanted level is high enough to bring them out — and survive the heat that follows. It can be tried again any time tanks are on the streets. Exactly what the game wants you to do in the Rhino is not pinned down by the official description, so treat getting in one and staying alive as the goal.

trophies.name: Sneakthief
trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store without being detected — a clean, quiet job. Case the store, go in soft, take the goods and leave before anyone raises the alarm. A blown attempt can be retried at another store or another time. Which jewelry stores can be robbed is not pinned down by the official description.

trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
trophies.guide: Rob 5 bank vaults and escape — the count the official list tracks. Each vault is its own job: get in, crack it, get out clean, and repeat at five different vaults. Vaults stay robbable, so this is a series of heists, not a one-shot. Where the vaults are is not pinned down by the official description.

trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Rob an armored truck and escape. Armored trucks run routes around the map, so find one on the road, stop it, take the cash and lose the heat that follows. Trucks keep running, so a failed attempt can be retried on the next one. The trucks' routes are not pinned down by the official description.

trophies.name: The Goodtime State
trophies.guide: Explore all of Leonida — the list tracks 52 areas. Drive, fly and walk into every corner of the map until all 52 areas register as visited. Nothing is locked away after the story, so take it as a road trip once the plot is done and use the map to find the gaps. Which places make up the 52 areas is not pinned down by the official description beyond the count.

trophies.name: Pest Control
trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob an illegal operation belonging to each gang — the list tracks 9 gangs. Find one operation per gang, hit it and move on to the next gang's turf. Operations stay available, so this is a tour of the underworld rather than a timed run. Which gangs hold which operations is not pinned down by the official description.

trophies.name: In The Beginning…
trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach. Head to a bar or venue on Ocean Beach, order a cocktail and take in the view — a quiet moment trophy, and one of the easiest in the list. The venue is not pinned down by the official description, so any Ocean Beach spot that serves a cocktail with a view should do.

trophies.name: Capital Offense
trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style — drive a car straight through the showroom glass, the way the series has always done it. Pick a showroom, get a car inside or lined up at the glass, and floor it. It can be retried at any showroom. Which showrooms work is not pinned down by the official description.

trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Follow through at the Kolt & Associates bowling alley — play a round of bowling there. The description names the alley, so go to Kolt & Associates, take to the lane and finish a game. One full game is the safe reading of the requirement. The alley's exact spot is not pinned down by the official description beyond its name.

trophies.name: Personal Best
trophies.guide: The description is deliberately cryptic: a partnership with mass appeal. It reads as a moment with your partner that the public notices — most likely a stunt or a scene the two of you pull off together that draws a crowd. Play the partner missions and free-roam moments with your partner and it should land. What exactly triggers it is not pinned down by the official description, so no specific step is claimed here.

trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
trophies.missableReason: Tied to choices made while playing — treat each choice as final; the official description does not say choices can be revisited.
trophies.guide: The description counts choices — PlayStation tracks a count toward 500 — so this is about the choices you make across the game, for better or worse. Keep playing and choosing; the count climbs with the decisions the game offers, in missions, strands and the open world. Which choices count is not pinned down by the official description, so the safest play is to take every choice the game offers rather than skipping dialogue or scenes.

trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
trophies.guide: Second time's the charm: succeed at something on the second try. The natural reading is to fail an attempt at something, then succeed at the very next try. It is a trophy that finds you — fail a race, a challenge or a mission objective, then win the retry. What exactly it counts is not pinned down by the official description, so no specific step is claimed here.

trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
trophies.guide: The description is a reaction, not an instruction: something strange happens and you are there to see it. This reads as a random world event or an odd encounter somewhere in Leonida — the kind of thing you stumble on while exploring. Keep your eyes open in the open world, especially off the beaten path. What the event is and where it happens is not pinned down by the official description, so no location is claimed here.

trophies.name: Ten Pin
trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Bowl them over with a melee drive-by — knock someone down with a melee attack from a moving vehicle. Drive slowly past a pedestrian and swing as you pass. It can be retried as often as you like, so take it slow and line the swing up. The exact speed and weapon are not pinned down by the official description.

trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts. Marked Bills come from robberies and heists, and your contacts turn them into clean money — keep feeding bills through them until the total hits $250,000. It is a long money grind that pairs with the robbery trophies. Which contacts launder bills is not pinned down by the official description.

trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 across all shops. Buy weapons, clothes, cars and anything else the shops sell — the total is cumulative across every shop, so normal spending while you play counts toward it. Big-ticket items like vehicles close the gap fastest. The shop list is not pinned down by the official description, but every shop in the game counts.

trophies.name: Little Boxes
trophies.guide: Purchase all garage properties — the list tracks 8 of them. Garages are bought through the in-game property market, so save up and buy each one as it becomes available. They stay for sale, so nothing here can be missed. Where the 8 garages sit is not pinned down by the official description.

trophies.name: On the Spot
trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app. Scooter Bros is the game's vehicle service app on the in-game phone, so open it and register ten different vehicles you own or find. The count is cumulative, so register vehicles as you collect them. How registration works in the app is not pinned down by the official description.
